newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares end up on economic data.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares end up on economic data.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed higher on Monday with shares moving in response to a steep rise in the A share market which was boosted by positive forecasts on the economy, brokers said.

The A share index surged 15.59 points or 4.08 percent to end at 398.22, with turnover rising to 11.12 billion yuan from Friday's 9.54 billion yuan. The index has risen for seven trading days in a row.
The B share index finished up 2.49 points or 1.62 percent at 155.63 on turnover of HK$108.26 million against HK$87 million.
"The advance was based on optimism about China's 1997 economic outlook," Xu Yinhui, an analyst with China Guotai Securities Co Ltd, said.
China's 1997 budget was announced in Beijing on Sunday, and included a gross domestic product (GDP) growth target of 8.0 percent and a retail price inflation target of 6.0 percent.
"Beijing is likely to lower bank interest rates if it is confident of capping retail price inflation below six percent," Xu said.
In 1996, China cut bank interest rates twice in May and August.
"I expect share prices to rise further during the annual company report season, before April 30," a second analyst said.
Some brokers said recent trading in A shares had been heavily speculative and a correction was sorely needed.
"Profit-taking is likely to set in soon," a broker said.
On the B share market, retailer Shenzhen International Enterprise was the strongest performer, gaining HK$0.29 or 5.57 percent to HK$5.50 on trade of 680,100 shares.
Analysts said they expected the firm to post strong profits for 1996 on real estate investments.
Appliance maker Tsann Kuen traded most on 2.08 million shares, putting on HK$0.10 to HK$3.88.
On the A share market, buying focused on recently-listed firms which are expected to draft attractive dividend plans for 1996, brokers said.
